I am a widow, my husband passed away nearly 3 months ago. I have 9 sons and 2 daughters. My husband?s mother is also alive. My late husband was the owner of two houses. Some months prior to his death, my husband made me a joint owner in one of these properties. Upon the instructions of my late husband, a solicitor completed the legal paperwork and we both signed various documents in the presence of witnesses. After the death of my husband, my children requested a scholar to explain the rules of Islamic inheritance so we could distribute my husband?s wealth according to the Shariah. When the discussion arose about the joint ownership of one of the houses, the scholar was of the opinion that this transfer of joint ownership was not valid because it seemed to him that this was only done symbolically and not as a genuine gift. However, beside the legal paperwork there is no other document available to support or negate the intention of the deceased. The scholar also said that even if the above gift was genuine, this kind of gift is faasid because of the following rule of Hiba: ومن وهب شقصاً مشاعاً فالهبة فاسدةٌ، فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز ) الهداية شرح بداية المبتدي,ص225,ج3, الناشر المكتبة الإسلامية) Which in essence says, if the item is such that if it is divided it can still be of use, then it is not permissible to give it without dividing it. Such items are ?a plot of land, a big house...?. See Bahishti Zewar (link below) page 66 point 5 http://www.islamicbulletin.org/free_downloads/women/bahishti_4_5_6_7.pdf I would be grateful if you would clarify (a) whether a house in the UK falls within the category of divisible property; (b) whether according to the Shariah I am the rightful owner of 50% of the house which was in joint ownership between myself and my husband. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Inheritance & Will Question ID: 44054 Country: India Title: Property distribution Question: A person has 2 sons and 1 daughter. The elder son has 2 children and daughter is married. The younger son has no children. The second son has adopted a female child and raised her. How do these 3 children distribute father's property? Dose the adopted child get any property? If the adopted child is not entitled for property, what is she eligible for? Dose the wife of childless son get any property? Answer ID: 44054 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 262/212/H=1434) The person has full power on his property during his lifetime. On his death if he left heirs then all the property shall be divided into 5 shares within them after due right proceeding inheritance. Out of which 2-2 shares shall go to each son and one share to the daughter. The grandsons, granddaughters shall get nothing. The adopted girl of the son shall also get nothing. Rather if the son who has adopted the girl dies then too the adopted girl shall get nothing in his property. However, if the said person or his son gifts something in their lifetime and gives it the possession of the girl then she shall become it owner. And there is no harm in this gift as per the Shariah. In short, she is not entitled to receive any thing in inheritance. However, it is allowable to give her something as gift. After she takes it into her possession she shall become its owner. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
